C10_venue_evidence.note: the brief asks for the venue of every fixture transcribed from the official game centre. Two were read this round; the other eleven are blank with 'not read this round', because the weekly schedule page prints no venue field and this repository does not infer one. The stadium-name disagreement on Colts at Texans is a finding, not a transcription error: both strings are printed by the NFL, on two different pages, for the same fixture.

C11_second_reader_agreement.note: the strongest check in this pack. Two transcriptions of the same four official pages, made independently minutes apart by different sessions with different column layouts, agreeing on every comparable cell - including 64 cells of a hand-typed injury spot-check against a full-page read neither one knew the other was making
C11_second_reader_agreement.what_the_parallel_read_withholds: its standings file omits DIV PCT and CONF PCT because that read could not separate them from the adjacent cell; this pack prints both, so those two columns are cross-checked against the collector read (C5) and not against this reader

C12_third_reader_agreement.coverage_note: the third reader transcribed all 347 injury rows on the page, against this pack's 44 hand-typed spot-check rows; the comparison covers the intersection, and the remaining 303 rows are checked against the retained capture by C8 rather than against a human
C12_third_reader_agreement.identifier_finding: the values agree on every cell; the identifiers do not. This pack spells the two clubs as the page prints them (LA, AZ) and the third read uses the nflverse-style codes (LAR, ARI) in its game_id while keeping LA/AZ in its own value columns. Any future join between these two trees must go through the fixture slug, not game_id, and the flag R1-08 exists to keep that from being discovered the hard way
C12_third_reader_agreement.kickoff_times_note: this pack prints time_et blank for a final because the schedule page does not reprint it; the third read sourced kickoff windows and networks for the same games from the injury hub's game-day headers, which is a different official page for the same fact - recorded here so the two packs' apparent disagreement on a blank is not read as one of them being incomplete

C3_league_closure.note: 136 games (weeks 1-9, data/results/_raw/reads.tsv) + the 14 Week 10 finals read today = the corpus the standings imply, to the game and to the point. C4_cross_page_records.note: a W-L-T printed beside a club on a schedule page has to equal the W-L-T on the standings page read separately; a transcription slip in either read shows up here
C4_cross_page_records.presentation_mapping: a card prints '8-1' for a club with no ties and '3-5-1' for one with a tie; the standings table prints three fields always. Compared as (W,L,T) with the missing field read as zero.

C5_independent_standings_reread.note: two reads of one official page by different code three hours apart, compared on all 16 printed columns. A pass means the collector and this transcription see the same table; it does not mean the page is right.

C5b_pinned_reference_is_stale.note: tools/verify_official.py fails on these cells and it is meant to: it compares a published table against a reference transcription three days older, and the league table moved in between. The 2026-11-17 read agrees with the collector on every cell (C5), so the disagreement is the pin's age, not a wrong published value. The pin belongs to another round's tree and is not refreshed here.

C6a_week11_slate_delta_vs_2026_11_16.records_moved_note: records are not in the tuple above on purpose: they are the cells expected to move when a game closes, so the slate check asks only whether the SLATE moved

C6b_week10_closure_delta_vs_2026_11_16.note: the 2026-11-16 read had 13 finals and the Monday-night game printed as Scheduled; today the page prints 14 finals. C7_results_log_gap.note: the published results log stops at the 2026-11-12 Thursday game.
